sections.title: Top level
sections.doc:
The root of rules.yaml: instance identity, sync interval,
operator notifications, provider accounts, and sync rules. Parsing is
strict — unknown fields are startup errors — and secrets never appear
here: account fields name environment variable identifiers, resolved at
startup from wherever the deployment sources them (a Kubernetes Secret,
.env locally).

fields.name: instance
fields.doc:
This Meridian instance's identity, embedded in every
ownership marker it writes. Must be unique across any instances
sharing a destination, and stable for the instance's lifetime —
changing it orphans every shadow the instance previously wrote (they
become invisible to it; `meridian wipe calendar <calendar> --instance
<old>` cleans them up).

fields.name: interval
fields.doc: The time between reconciliation cycles.

fields.name: webhookURLEnv
fields.doc:
Names the env var holding a webhook URL to POST
notifications to, as `{"content": "..."}` — Discord's incoming-webhook
shape, so one of those URLs needs nothing in front of it.
Empty/unset disables notifications, which is the normal setup under
Kubernetes: guard triggers and auth failures emit metrics and logs
either way, and those are what an alerting stack is already watching.

sections.title: `guards`
sections.doc:
Tunes the hardening guards. Everything here governs detection, not
blocking: a guard records what it saw and the cycle proceeds.

fields.name: massDeleteFraction
fields.doc:
Triggers the mass-delete guard
(meridian_guard_triggers_total{guard="mass_delete"}) when a rule
deletes more than this fraction of its shadows in one cycle. The
trigger also sends a notification when one is configured, but the
metric and the log fire either way. 0 disables the guard.

sections.title: `accounts`
sections.doc:
One provider connection. Type-specific fields are validated
per type; setting a field that belongs to the other type is a startup
error.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
The account's unique name, referenced in rules as
`<account>/<calendar>`.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: Selects the provider: google or caldav.

fields.name: endpoint
fields.doc: The CalDAV server's base URL.

fields.name: usernameEnv
fields.doc: Names the env var holding the CalDAV Basic Auth username.

fields.name: passwordEnv
fields.doc:
Names the env var holding the CalDAV Basic Auth password
(an app-specific password, if the provider requires 2FA).

fields.name: clientIDEnv
fields.doc: Names the env var holding the Google OAuth client ID.

fields.name: clientSecretEnv
fields.doc:
Names the env var holding the Google OAuth client
secret.

fields.name: refreshTokenEnv
fields.doc:
Names the env var holding a long-lived Google OAuth
refresh token. Get one via `meridian oauth`.

fields.name: identities
fields.doc:
The calendar addresses this server knows the account
owner by, used to read the owner's own RSVP off an invitation.
Google needs none — the API marks the owner's attendee entry — so
this is CalDAV-only, where iCalendar has no such marker. Usually one
address; `meridian identities <account>` asks the server for it.

Only addresses belonging to THIS account. A calendar mirrored in from
elsewhere carries the owner's address on that other system, which the
server won't report; add it here by hand to read RSVP off such a
calendar.

sections.title: `accounts[].calendars`
sections.doc:
Names one calendar of an account. The logical reference
used in rules is `<account>/<calendar>`.

fields.name: name
fields.doc:
Unique within the account; combines with the account name
as `<account>/<name>` in rules.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: The CalDAV collection path.

fields.name: id
fields.doc:
The Google Calendar ID: "primary", or
"xxxx@group.calendar.google.com" from Settings -> Integrate calendar.

sections.title: `rules`
sections.doc:
One sync rule (compiled into sync.Rule). A destination
calendar can be targeted by any number of rules simultaneously —
ownership is scoped by instance + rule ID, so rules never fight over
each other's shadows.

fields.name: id
fields.doc:
Unique across the whole config, embedded in every shadow's
ownership marker. Renaming a rule is equivalent to deleting it and
creating a new one: old shadows get swept as orphans, new ones get
created fresh.

fields.name: from
fields.doc:
The source `<account>/<calendar>` reference; must be a
configured calendar.

fields.name: to
fields.doc:
Lists destination `<account>/<calendar>` references; none may
equal From.

fields.name: filter
fields.doc:
Selects which source events this rule mirrors. Unset matches
every event in the sync window.

fields.name: transform
fields.doc:
Computes the shadow's content. Unset mirrors every field
faithfully.

sections.title: `filter`
sections.doc:
Selects source events. All set fields AND together: an
event must satisfy every one to match.

fields.name: weekdays
fields.doc:
A subset of mon..sun. All-day events are matched by
their date against this list alone — never subject to Window.

fields.name: window
fields.doc:
A daily time-of-day range ("HH:MM-HH:MM", must not cross
midnight), evaluated in Timezone. An event matches if it overlaps
the window on a matching weekday.

fields.name: timezone
fields.doc:
An IANA zone name, required whenever Window or Weekdays
is set — event times are UTC instants internally, so this is what
makes the wall-clock window meaningful.

fields.name: skipTransparent
fields.doc:
Skips events marked transparent ("free") at the
source.

fields.name: skipAllDay
fields.doc: Skips all-day events entirely.

fields.name: skipDeclined
fields.doc:
Skips invitations the calendar owner declined. Events
the owner was never invited to are unaffected, so this never touches
ordinary non-meeting events. CalDAV sources need account.identities
for the owner's response to be readable at all.

fields.name: when
fields.doc:
A CEL expression over the CELEvent schema, ANDed with every
other set field. Compiled and type-checked at config load — a bad
expression is a startup error, never a mid-sync surprise.

sections.title: `transform`
sections.doc:
Computes the shadow's content. Every field left unset
copies the corresponding source value (faithful mirror by default); it
only needs to name what should differ. Deliberately not
expression-powered the way filter.when is: a bad filter mis-selects
events, but a bad transform corrupts calendar data, so string fields get
templating and nothing more.

fields.name: title
fields.doc:
A literal string or a Go template
(https://pkg.go.dev/text/template) over the source event; the
literal "drop" empties it instead of copying or templating it.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: Follows the same rules as Title.

fields.name: location
fields.doc: Follows the same rules as Title.

fields.name: transparent
fields.doc:
Forces the shadow's opacity regardless of the source
event's own transparency; unset copies the source's value.

fields.name: transparentForRSVP
fields.doc:
Lists the responses (needsAction, accepted,
declined, tentative) whose copies stop blocking time, so a meeting
still sitting unanswered shows up without holding the slot. Any other
response keeps the source's own transparency, and an event the owner
was never invited to is untouched. Mutually exclusive with
`transparent`, which forces one answer for every event.

fields.name: reminders
fields.doc:
A list of minutes before start; an empty list means no
reminders. Unset copies the source's reminders.

fields.name: color
fields.doc:
Has no source value to copy, so unset means no override at
all, not "mirror the source's color". Encoding is
destination-provider-specific — see the rules cookbook.

fields.name: visibility
fields.doc:
Sets who may read the shadow: public, private or
confidential. Unset mirrors the source. Independent of Transparent,
which governs whether the shadow blocks time rather than who sees it.
Not templated: a closed set is worth more here than an expression
free to produce a value no provider accepts.

celEventSchema.title: CEL event schema
celEventSchema.doc:
The documented, versioned event schema exposed to filter.when
expressions. Field names come from the cel tags; this is a public API —
extend, never rename.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: The event's title.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: The event's description.

fields.name: location
fields.doc: The event's location.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: The event's start instant.

fields.name: end
fields.doc: The event's end instant.

fields.name: durationMinutes
fields.doc: End minus Start, in minutes.

fields.name: allDay
fields.doc: True for all-day (DATE-valued) events.

fields.name: transparent
fields.doc: True when the source marks the event as free.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The event's status (e.g. confirmed, tentative, cancelled).

fields.name: visibility
fields.doc:
The event's disclosure class: public, private,
confidential, or empty when the source inherits its calendar default.

fields.name: organizer
fields.doc: The event organizer's identifier.

fields.name: attendees
fields.doc: Lists attendee identifiers.

fields.name: rsvp
fields.doc:
The calendar owner's own response to an invitation:
needsAction, accepted, declined or tentative. Empty when the owner
has no attendee record, which is every event that isn't an
invitation — test for a specific value, never for "not accepted",
or the expression also catches ordinary non-meeting events.
